fact_en: Soil has cool layers! The dark, nutrient-rich topsoil is on top, subsoil is below it, and solid bedrock is at the very bottom.
fact_bis: Ang yuta adunay mga sapaw! Ang itom nga nutrient-rich topsoil sa ibabaw, subsoil sa kinaadman, ug solid bedrock sa pinakaubos.

findings.note: Body: "topsoil sa ibabaw, subsoil SA KINAADMAN, ug solid bedrock sa pinakaubos". Kinaadman = wisdom/knowledge, not a place; the English is "subsoil is below it" (ilawom / kahiladman — likely a corruption of kahiladman, "the depths"). This card's whole point is the ORDER of the layers, and the middle layer's position word is nonsense; a child can only infer it from the list order.

fact_en: Soil forms super slowly! It can take hundreds of years just to build one thin layer of rich topsoil.
fact_bis: Hinay kaayo ang pagporma sa yuta! Mahimong moabot og gatusan ka tuig aron makahimo lang og usa ka nipis nga sapaw sa rich topsoil.

findings.note: title_bis "Hinay nga Pagbuto sa Yuta" = "the soil's slow EXPLOSION" (buto = blow up; the same batch uses "mibuto" for Pinatubo erupting). English title is "Slow Soil Formation", and the card's own body has the correct word — "Hinay kaayo ang pagporma sa yuta". Classic title-outlier: the body says pagporma, only the heading says pagbuto.

fact_en: A go-bag holds emergency essentials like food, water, medicine, important documents, and a flashlight! Always prepare yours before a typhoon arrives.
fact_bis: Ang go-bag adunay mga emergency essentials sama sa pagkain, tubig, gamot, importante nga dokumento, ug flashlight! I-andam kini sa wala pa moabot ang bagyo.

findings.note: Go-bag contents list "pagkain, tubig, gamot, importante nga dokumento, ug flashlight" — English is "medicine". In Cebuano gamot = ROOT (medicine = tambal), the confirmed false friend, and nothing else in the card restores "medicine". Same-batch evidence: ffct-32495 ("Roots Hold the Soil") uses gamot correctly for roots, so this corpus really does mean root by gamot. A child packing a go-bag from this card loses the medicine item.

fact_en:
Why do monsoon winds change direction twice a year?

It's because of land and sea temperatures! In summer, hotter land pulls wind from the sea. In winter, warmer sea reverses the wind!
fact_bis:
Nganong nagbag-o og direksyon ang monsoon winds makaduha sa usa ka tuig?

Tungod sa temperatura sa yuta ug dagat! Sa ting-init, mas init ang yuta mao nga mohuyop ang hangin gikan sa dagat. Sa ting-ulan, mas mainit ang dagat mao nga mag-reverse ang hangin!

findings.note: "Sa ting-init ... mohuyop ang hangin gikan sa dagat. Sa ting-ulan, mas mainit ang dagat mao nga mag-reverse ang hangin" — English says "In winter, warmer sea reverses the wind". Ting-ulan is the RAINY season, not winter (tingtugnaw, which ffct-32537 in this same batch uses correctly for winter). The card therefore puts the monsoon reversal in the wet season, i.e. exactly when the habagat blows in FROM the sea — a reversed season/direction fact that nothing in the card corrects, and it contradicts ffct-32463 (amihan = Dec-Feb).

fact_en:
Why are river floodplains great for farming?

River floodplains are very fertile farmland because of rich sediment deposited by rivers! However, these areas still have a high risk of flooding.
fact_bis:
Nganong maayo ang mga river floodplains alang sa pagsasaka?

Ang mga river floodplains maayo kaayo nga farmland tungod sa rich sediment gikan sa suba! Apan, taas gihapon ang risk of flooding sa mga lugar nga kini.

findings.note: title_bis "Matabang Floodplain" for "Fertile Floodplains". Matabang is the Tagalog import (lupang mataba/matabang = fertile); in Cebuano it reads as bland/tasteless (tab-ang) or helpful (tabang), never fertile — Cebuano fertile soil is tabunok. Lower severity than the three above: title-only, and the body paraphrases the idea as "maayo kaayo nga farmland tungod sa rich sediment" without ever using tabunok.

fact_en: A double rainbow happens when light reflects twice inside water droplets! The second rainbow is fainter and has its colors in reverse order.
fact_bis: Mahitabo ang double rainbow sa dihang mag-reflect og makaduha ang kahayag sulod sa water droplets! Mas mapusyaw ang ikaduha ug binalikbalik ang ayos sa kolor.

findings.note: EN: the second rainbow 'has its colors in reverse order'. Bis says 'binalikbalik ang ayos sa kolor', which reads as the order being repeated/done over and over, not reversed (Cebuano for reversed is balit-ad/baliktad — this same corpus uses 'balit-ad' correctly in ffct-32613). The reversal is the card's distinguishing fact and nothing else in the card restores it. Lower confidence than the other two: a sympathetic reader may still take 'balik' as 'flipped back'.

fact_en:
How did old-time Filipinos predict the weather?

They watched natural signs! 'A ring around the moon means rain' and 'many ants moving means rain is coming' — modern science confirms some of these!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagtagna sa atong mga katigulangan sa panahon?

Nagtan-aw sila sa mga natural nga palatandaan! 'Ang singsing palibot sa buwan nagpasabot og ulan' ug 'daghang langgam nga nagbalhin nagpasabot og ulan' — gipamatud-an sa modernong siyensya ang pipila niini!

findings.note: EN folk sign is 'many ants moving means rain is coming'; bis says 'daghang langgam nga nagbalhin nagpasabot og ulan'. In Cebuano langgam = BIRD (ant = hulmigas/guyam) — the confirmed Tagalog false friend. Nothing in the card corrects it, and the terms list even carries the bad mapping ("ants", "langgam"), so a child learns a different weather sign (migrating birds) than the card teaches.

fact_en:
Why is it so important to keep trees and grass on Philippine mountains?

Heavy rain on steep slopes washes away fertile topsoil through erosion! Trees and grass hold the soil in place.
fact_bis:
Nganong importante kaayo nga magpabilin ang mga kahoy ug balili sa mga bukid sa Pilipinas?

Ang kusog nga ulan sa mga dik-as nga daplin nagkuha sa mataba nga topsoil pinaagi sa erosion!

findings.note: Q&A card: the Cebuano question asks 'Nganong importante kaayo nga magpabilin ang mga kahoy ug balili sa mga bukid?' but the answer only states that heavy rain on steep slopes strips topsoil via erosion. The EN answer's second sentence — 'Trees and grass hold the soil in place' — is dropped entirely, so the Cebuano never links trees/grass to holding soil and the card's own question is left unanswered.

fact_en: Obsidian is a black glassy rock that forms when lava cools so rapidly that no crystals can grow. It is extremely sharp and was used by ancient people for tools and weapons!
fact_bis: Ang obsidian usa ka itom nga glassy rock nga naporma kon ang lava kusog kaayong nagbugnaw nga walay pagkahigayon nga motubo ang mga kristal. Grabe ka hait kini ug gigamit sa mga karaan nga tawo sa mga himan ug armas!

findings.note: title_en "Sharp Obsidian Glass" -> title_bis "Obsidian nga Matarong". `matarong` = righteous/upright (moral), never sharp; Cebuano for sharp is `hait` — which this card's OWN body uses ("Grabe ka hait kini"), so the title is the outlier. Systematic in the corpus: ffct-13345 "Fovea Matarong" and ffct-02597 "Matarong nga Ngipon sa Karniboro" repeat the same swap.

fact_en:
What kind of rock do Philippine volcanoes make?

Andesite is a common volcanic rock in Ring of Fire volcanoes, including those in the Philippines! It is thicker (more viscous) than basalt and can produce more explosive eruptions.
fact_bis:
Unang klase sa bato ang gihimo sa mga bulkan sa Pilipinas?

Ang andesite usa ka komon nga volcanic rock sa mga bulkan sa Ring of Fire, lakip ang mga sa Pilipinas! Kini mas baga (viscous) kaysa basalt ug mahimong maghatag og mas mapuslanon nga mga pagsabog.

findings.note: EN: andesite "can produce more explosive eruptions". BIS: "mahimong maghatag og mas mapuslanon nga mga pagsabog" = more USEFUL/beneficial eruptions. `mapuslanon` means useful/advantageous everywhere else in this corpus (138 cards). Nothing else in the card says explosive or dangerous, so a Cebuano-only reader learns the opposite of the hazard point the card exists to make. Correct: "mas kusog/mabungrot nga pagsabog".

fact_en: When shaking starts: DUCK down, COVER your head under a sturdy table, and HOLD ON tight! Never run outside while the ground is shaking.
fact_bis: Kung nayanig: DUCK (magtaob), COVER ang ulo ubos sa lig-on nga lamesa, ug HOLD ON nga hugot! Ayaw dagan palabas samtang nayanig pa.

findings.note: Safety card. EN "DUCK down" is glossed in BIS as "DUCK (magtaob)". In Cebuano `taob` is the rising/high TIDE (96 cards in this corpus use it that way: "pagtaob ug paghunas sa dagat") — it is the Tagalog false friend of *taob* (face-down/overturned). The gloss is the only explanation of the action and points up, not down; correct is `duko` / `moduko`.

fact_en:
Where can you find one of the world's biggest geothermal power plants?

MakBan in Laguna and Batangas is one of the largest geothermal complexes in the Philippines and the world! It uses hot steam from underground near Mt. Makiling and Mt. Banahaw.
fact_bis:
Asa ang labing dagkong geothermal complex sa kalibutan?

Ang MakBan sa Laguna ug Batangas, Pilipinas! Naggamit kini og mainit nga steam gikan sa ilalom sa yuta duol sa Mt. Makiling ug Mt. Banahaw.

findings.note: EN hedges twice: "one of the world's biggest geothermal power plants" / "MakBan ... is one of the largest geothermal complexes in the Philippines and the world". The Cebuano drops the hedge in BOTH places: the question becomes "Asa ang labing dagkong geothermal complex sa kalibutan?" (where is the world's LARGEST) and the answer is flatly "Ang MakBan sa Laguna ug Batangas, Pilipinas!" — the clause "usa sa labing dagko" appears nowhere. A Cebuano-only child learns MakBan is the single largest geothermal complex on Earth, which is false and unrecoverable from the card. Same defect class as gold row ffct-17976 (quantifier dropped -> class-wide claim).
